alternate_names: Bangaru Kamakshi (the golden image now at Thanjavur)
deities: Kamakshi Amman (Parvati, as Lalita Tripurasundari; seated in yogic posture)
Sri Chakra / Sri Yantra (installed by Adi Shankaracharya)

history.period: Origins uncertain (antiquity); Pallava-era origins commonly cited
history.summary: The Kamakshi Amman Temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (the navel of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen here) and, with Madurai Meenakshi and Varanasi Vishalakshi, one of the three most important Shakti temples of India. Tradition attributes its building to the Pallava kings with later Chola and Vijayanagara expansions; the exact origins are lost to antiquity. Adi Shankaracharya is said to have installed the Sri Yantra here to stabilize the goddess's intense energy, and the temple is closely associated with the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham. Legend holds that Kamakshi performed penance standing on one leg atop a needle amidst fire, and married Shiva as Ekambareswarar at Kanchipuram. Note: a YouTube travel source claims 'only Hindus allowed inside' and 'built in 6th century AD by Pallava kings' - neither claim is corroborated by other sources; verify.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
town_description: Kanchipuram, about 72 km southwest of Chennai, is one of Hinduism's seven holiest cities (Sapta Puri) and the 'City of a Thousand Temples', famed for Shiva and Vishnu temples and its silk sarees.

travel.airport: Chennai International Airport, about 75 km away.
travel.railway: Kanchipuram Railway Station, about 1 km from the temple (per travel sources).
travel.road: About 72 km from Chennai via NH48; TNSTC and private buses run regularly.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 am - 12:15 pm and 4:00 pm - 8:15 pm (till 9:30 pm on Fridays and 10:30 pm on Pournami, per yatradham.org). Note: aanmeegam.org lists an entirely different schedule (e.g. 6:00 am - 1:30 pm and 3:00 pm - 9:30 pm) - verify on visit.
